newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 14.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- Park Chan-jong, a presidential aspirant of the ruling New Korea Party, held a news conference on Sunday claiming some of his competitors are buying votes of party representatives ahead of the national convention to elect a presidential candidate.
- Former U.S. ambassdor to South Korea James Laney and former senator Sam Nunn will fly into North Korea on July 19 to stay until July 22.

- Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) contracted a North Korean construction company to build a road connecting the northern port of Shinpo and Kumho where new light-water reactors will be built. KEPCO offered to provide breakfast and lunch for North Korean workers, but the North said it would only accept lunch.
- Five U.S. industry associations have recently taken issue with what they allege are import barriers in Korea, Seoul officials said.
